# National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) Summary
Founded on September 22, 1910, UNAM was established by Justo Sierra to be a secular, national, and positivist institution, distinct from its 19th-century predecessor, the Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico. The university initially integrated various decentralized colleges in Mexico City, unifying fields such as Fine Arts, Business, Political Science, Jurisprudence, Engineering, Medicine, and Normal schools. Over time, UNAM gained autonomy, culminating in the consolidation onto the new campus, Ciudad Universitaria, in the 1950s.
UNAM is organized into schools or colleges, with both undergraduate and graduate studies available across its offerings. The university hosts a large student body and is known for its politically active student population. Notable achievements include securing the Prince of Asturias Award for Communication and Humanities in 2009. Its cultural identity is reflected in its seal, designed by José Vasconcelos, which features a Mexican eagle and an Andean condor, and its motto, "For my people the spirit shall speak."
